questions.question: Which of the following is NOT compulsory equipment for a football referee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**White flag**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **White flag** is not a compulsory piece of equipment for a football referee.
 
• Essential equipment for a football referee includes items such as **watch(es), whistle(s), and red and yellow cards**.
 
• These tools help the referee manage the game, keep time, and enforce the rules effectively.
 
• Other non-compulsory items may be used at the referee's discretion but are not mandated by the official regulations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Laws of the Game** are established by the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and specify the required equipment for referees.
 
• Referees must carry a **whistle** to signal the start and stop of play, and **red and yellow cards** to discipline players.
 
• They must also have a **watch** to keep track of the match time and any additional time to be added.
 
• While other items like notebooks, pens, and coin for the toss are commonly used, they are also not strictly compulsory.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classical languages of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magahi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magahi** is not one of the classical languages of India.
 
• The classical languages of India include **Kannada, Malayalam, Odiya, Tamil, Sanskrit, and Telugu**.
 
• A language is declared as a classical language based on its rich heritage and independent tradition.
 
• The criteria for classical language status include antiquity of early texts/recorded history over a period of 1500-2000 years and a body of ancient literature or texts, which is considered a valuable heritage by generations of speakers.
 
• Recognition as a classical language also involves a distinction between the classical language and its modern form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kannada** was declared a classical language in 2008.
 
• **Malayalam** received its classical language status in 2013.
 
• **Odiya** was granted classical language status in 2014.
 
• The first language to be declared as classical in India was **Tamil** in 2004.
 
• **Sanskrit** and **Telugu** are also recognized as classical languages, having been declared in 2005 and 2008 respectively.
 
• The Union Cabinet approved the inclusion of **Marathi, Assamese, Bengali, Pali, and Prakrit,** raising the count from **six to eleven.** These additions reflect the expanding understanding of India's rich linguistic heritage in **October 2024.**

questions.question: Select the natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gir forest**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gir forest** is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica).
 
• Located in the state of **Gujarat, India**, the Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary is the last refuge of the Asiatic Lion.
 
• The park was established in **1965** and covers a total area of **1,412 square kilometers**.
 
• Conservation efforts in Gir have been successful in increasing the population of Asiatic Lions from a mere **20 in the early 20th century** to over **500 today**.
 
• The ecosystem of Gir forest is unique, supporting a rich biodiversity that includes leopards, deer, antelopes, and numerous bird species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Asiatic Lion** once roamed across the Middle East and India but is now restricted to the Gir forest.
 
• The Government of India and the Gujarat state government have implemented several **conservation programs** to protect the Asiatic Lion.
 
• In addition to Gir, there are efforts to identify and establish **alternative habitats** to ensure a healthy and genetically diverse population.
 
• The Gir forest is also a significant cultural and historical site, attracting numerous **tourists** and wildlife enthusiasts from around the world.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT related to the ‘Trinity of Carnatic Music’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purandara Das**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Syama Shastri**, **Tyagaraja**, and **Muthuswami Dikshitar** are considered the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music'.
 
• They are renowned composers and are highly revered in the Carnatic music tradition.
 
• **Purandara Das** is not part of this trinity. Although he is a significant figure in Carnatic music, he lived earlier and is often referred to as the "father of Carnatic music."
 
• The contributions of the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music' have had a profound influence on the development and propagation of Carnatic music.
 
• Their compositions are still widely performed and form a crucial part of the Carnatic music repertoire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Syama Shastri** (1762–1827), **Tyagaraja** (1767–1847), and **Muthuswami Dikshitar** (1775–1835) were contemporaries and their works have been foundational in Carnatic music.
 
• They have composed thousands of kritis (songs) that are still sung and cherished by Carnatic musicians and enthusiasts alike.
 
• Their compositions are known for their intricate melodies, rich rhythmic patterns, and deep devotion.
 
• **Purandara Das** (1484–1564) is credited with systematizing the teaching of Carnatic music and composing thousands of devotional songs known as "Devaranamas".

questions.question: Which statement about Classical Carnatic Music is correct?

options.text: The compositions are either in Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil or Bengali.
The compositions are either in Marathi, Odia, Konkani or Bengali.
The compositions are either in Telugu, Malayalam, Hindi or Sanskrit.
The compositions are either in Telugu, Kannada, Tamil or Sanskrit.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The compositions are either in Telugu, Kannada, Tamil or Sanskrit**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The compositions in Classical Carnatic Music are either in **Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, or Sanskrit.**
 
• Carnatic music, known for its intricate and complex compositions, primarily uses these languages for its lyrics and vocal performances.
 
• These languages have a rich history and are deeply embedded in the cultural and musical traditions of South India.
 
• The compositions often reflect religious themes, devotional content, and classical poetry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic music** is a major system of Indian classical music that originated in the southern part of India.
 
• It is known for its fixed compositions and a high degree of improvisation within the structure of the raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic cycles).
 
• The compositions are usually set to a specific raga and tala, and are performed with a high level of technical proficiency and emotional expression.
 
• Some of the most renowned composers in Carnatic music include **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri.**

questions.question: Price control and rationing are direct control measures to check ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**inflation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Price control** and **rationing** are direct measures used by governments to manage and control **inflation**.
 
• Inflation refers to the general increase in prices and the fall in the purchasing value of money.
 
• Price control involves setting a maximum price level for essential goods to prevent them from becoming unaffordable during high inflation periods.
 
• Rationing ensures the equitable distribution of scarce resources by limiting the amount of goods each individual can purchase.
 
• These measures are typically used in situations where inflation is driven by supply shortages or excessive demand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inflation control** is crucial for maintaining economic stability and ensuring the affordability of goods and services.
 
• Other measures to control inflation include monetary policy adjustments, such as increasing interest rates, and fiscal policies like reducing government spending.
 
• Governments may also use subsidies and tax reductions to offset the impact of rising prices on consumers.
 
• Effective inflation management helps in sustaining economic growth and protecting the purchasing power of the currency.
 
• Long-term inflation control strategies involve improving production efficiency and increasing the supply of goods and services.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Rights were initially provided in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seven Fundamental Rights** were initially provided in the Constitution of India.
 
• These Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35.
 
• They are considered essential for the protection of individual liberties and democratic principles in India.
 
• The original seven Fundamental Rights included the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, Right to Property, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• The Right to Property was later removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 and was made a constitutional legal right under Article 300A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning that individuals can approach the courts to seek enforcement of these rights.
 
• The Supreme Court and High Courts have the power to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• Fundamental Rights are subject to certain restrictions and can be suspended during a state of emergency, except the rights guaranteed under Articles 20 and 21.

questions.question: According to Koeppen's Scheme of classification of climate, which of the following characteristics is associated with 'Group E'?

options.text: The average temperature for all months is below 10°C
The average temperature of the coldest month is 18°C or higher
The average temperature of the coldest month is –3°C or below
The average temperature of the coldest month is higher than –3°C but below 18°C

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The average temperature for all months is below 10ºC**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The average temperature for all months is below 10ºC** is the characteristic associated with 'Group E' in Koeppen's Scheme of classification of climate.
 
• Koeppen's classification is a widely used system for categorizing the world's climates based on the annual and monthly averages of temperature and precipitation.
 
• 'Group E' represents polar climates, which are characterized by extremely low temperatures throughout the year.
 
• These climates are typically found in the polar regions, including Antarctica and the Arctic.
 
• Due to the harsh conditions, these regions have very limited vegetation and are often covered in ice and snow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Koeppen's Scheme** was developed by Wladimir Koeppen, a German climatologist, in the early 20th century.
 
• The classification system divides the world into five main climate groups: A (tropical), B (dry), C (temperate), D (continental), and E (polar).
 
• Each group is further divided based on specific criteria related to temperature and precipitation patterns.
 
• Koeppen's classification is still widely used in climatology, geography, and environmental studies due to its simplicity and effectiveness in describing climate zones.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct relationship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**F = ma**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 4** correctly represents the relationship as per Newton's second law of motion, which states that Force (F) is the product of Mass (m) and Acceleration (a).
 
• The formula **F = ma** is fundamental in classical mechanics and is used to calculate the force applied to an object when its mass and acceleration are known.
 
• Understanding this relationship is crucial for solving many problems in physics and engineering related to motion and force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's second law of motion** can be mathematically represented as **F = ma**, where:

 
 
• **F** is the force applied to the object.
 
• **m** is the mass of the object.
 
• **a** is the acceleration of the object.
 
 
 
• This law implies that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.
 
• It is a vector equation, meaning it considers both the magnitude and direction of the force and acceleration.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalbelia**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalbelia** dance is listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010.
 
• Kalbelia dance is associated with the Kalbelia tribe of Rajasthan, India, and is known for its graceful movements and traditional music.
 
• It is often referred to as the "snake charmer dance" due to its fluid and sinuous movements that resemble those of a serpent.
 
• The dance is performed by both men and women, with women wearing traditional black swirling skirts adorned with silver jewelry and embroidery.
 
• Musical accompaniment typically includes instruments like the 'pungi' (a woodwind instrument), 'dholak' (a two-headed hand drum), and 'khanjari' (a tambourine-like instrument).
 
• Kalbelia dance is an integral part of the cultural heritage of Rajasthan and reflects the nomadic lifestyle of the Kalbelia community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage aims to ensure the better protection of important cultural practices and expressions around the world.
 
• India has several other elements inscribed on the list, including Yoga, Kumbh Mela, and the tradition of Vedic chanting.
 
• The inclusion of cultural elements in the UNESCO list helps in the preservation and promotion of these traditions, ensuring they are passed down to future generations.
 
• Efforts are made by various organizations and the government to support and sustain these cultural practices through various initiatives and programs.

questions.question: Which sport is NOT played in mixed doubles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Handball**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Sports such as **tennis, table tennis, and badminton** have mixed doubles events.

questions.question: _________ of the Constitution of India has provisions for legal enforcement of the fundamental rights.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Constitution of India provides for the legal enforcement of the fundamental rights.
 
• It grants the right to individuals to approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• This article is often referred to as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, one of the principal architects of the Constitution.
 
• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court has the power to issue writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari, for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• It ensures that the fundamental rights of individuals are protected and can be enforced through the judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental rights** are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the overall development of individuals and are guaranteed against state actions.
 
• Article 32 is a crucial aspect of the Constitution as it provides a direct remedy for the violation of fundamental rights.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar emphasized the importance of Article 32, stating that without it, the Constitution would be a nullity.
 
• The Supreme Court of India, through its power under Article 32, acts as the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights.

questions.question: Application software includes a variety of programs that are designed to meet the information processing needs of _______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**end users**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **End users** are the primary beneficiaries of application software.
 
• Application software is designed to help **end users** perform specific tasks such as word processing, web browsing, and managing data.
 
• Other roles like **programmers** and **team leaders** may use application software, but the software is generally created with the needs of the **end users** in mind.
 
• Examples of application software include **Microsoft Office, Adobe Photoshop, and Google Chrome**, which are used by **end users** for various personal and professional activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **System software** differs from application software in that it is designed to manage system resources and provide a platform for application software to run.
 
• **Examples of system software** include operating systems like **Windows, macOS, and Linux**.
 
• Application software is generally more user-friendly and accessible to non-technical users compared to system software.
 
• With the rise of cloud computing, many application software solutions are now available as **Software as a Service (SaaS)**, which allows **end users** to access software applications over the internet.

questions.question: Which amongst the following Sultans shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Bin Tughlaq**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** was the Sultan who shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.
 
• This decision was made during his reign in the early 14th century.
 
• The move was intended to help control the Deccan region more effectively and to protect the capital from Mongol invasions.
 
• However, the decision proved to be a failure due to logistical issues and the hardships it caused to the people.
 
• Eventually, the capital was moved back to Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** ruled from 1325 to 1351 and is known for his ambitious but often impractical projects.
 
• He was the second ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• His reign is marked by several bold experiments in governance, including the introduction of token currency and tax reforms.
 
• Despite his intelligence and vision, many of his policies were considered ahead of their time and failed due to poor execution.
 
• His decision to shift the capital is often cited as a classic example of his ambitious but flawed administrative decisions.
